"One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity," sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. stories.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer

The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol.

How Black camp meetings grew from hushed gatherings into an enduring spiritual tradition
stories.summary: The meetings are part of ‘Black worldmaking that is spiritual and natural and familial and intergenerational’ A s the days shorten and the temperature cools, children run around a South Carolina camp ground in celebration of the harvest season. For more than 150 years, thousands of people altogether have congregated at St Paul camp ground in Dorchester county. stories.title: Parrots' vibrant feathers are surprisingly susceptible to bacterial attack
stories.summary: Flashy birds, from peacocks to parrots, have inspired a long tradition of using animal colors to study evolution. Colorful plumage often functions as a signal—for example, to attract a mate. Alternatively, drab colors can be used for camouflage. However, color can have functions beyond signaling and camouflage. This is because pigments, the molecules embedded in feather tissues to produce a broad range of colors, can also influence other aspects of feathers, ranging from mechanical strength to thermoregulatory properties.

Ancient climate records reveal how East Asian monsoon shifted abruptly into cold and drought
stories.summary: How does climate change affect the East Asian monsoon? Researchers from Utrecht University's Faculty of Geosciences, together with colleagues at research institutes in China and Belgium, are investigating this question by looking back 250,000 years. They found that, over long timescales, the monsoon system tracks changes in incoming solar radiation caused by variations in Earth's orbit and tilt. But when radiation falls below a certain threshold, abrupt periods of extreme cold and drought occur, particularly when atmospheric CO₂ concentrations are low. The study was published in Communications Earth & Environment.
